title: Existence of the contracted product of an etale torsor
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\varphi:G\to G^{\prime}$ a morphism of abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] on its small etale site, and $T$ a $G$-torsor [def-sc-gm-torsor]. There exists a $G^{\prime}$-torsor $T^{\prime}$ carrying a contracted-product presentation [def-sc-contracted-product-presentation]: it is the sheafification of the sectionwise orbit presheaf of $T\times G^{\prime}$ for $(g,t,h)\mapsto(g+ t,h-\varphi(g))$, with the natural invariant quotient map, translation by $G^{\prime}$ on the second factor, and the universal property against every sheaf of sets.

source.place: Tag 03AJ, label lemma-torsors-h1, fibre-of-a-section construction; contracted-product construction from lem-sc-etale-torsor-pushout-extension step 2; torsors as in Tag 03AH

proof.text: Form the sectionwise orbit presheaf and sheafify it using [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. Restriction respects the antidiagonal relation; the quotient map is natural and invariant. Translation in the second factor commutes with the relation and descends, then extends through sheafification.

On a covering where T has a section t0, each orbit has a unique representative (t0,h). This identifies the quotient sheaf locally with G prime and identifies its action with translation. Local nonemptiness and simple transitivity give the torsor axioms. This also applies to the zero group, zero coefficient map, and empty scheme.

A natural invariant map to a sheaf F factors uniquely through the orbit presheaf, by the set quotient universal property, and then uniquely through its sheafification, by [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. These factorizations, the invariant quotient map and its translation equation are exactly [def-sc-contracted-product-presentation].
